title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning to prevent queue starvation, improve fairness, and enforce timeouts
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: Scheduler tuning for continuous batcher: adds per-queue aging to prevent starvation, dynamic queue timeouts and backoff, improved fairness heuristics; exposes runtime knobs and metrics. Expected tail-latency improvement ~10-20% for mixed latency/throughput workloads. No API breaking changes.
description:
Summary: This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to address observed queue starvation and tail latency regressions under mixed workloads. Motivation: Customers running mixed short/long requests and multi-tenant workloads reported unfair queueing where small requests were delayed behind large KV-heavy requests. The continuous batcher needs better fairness and explicit timeouts to bound latency.

Implementation: 1) Per-queue priority aging: newly enqueued requests get an age counter that increases their effective priority over time to ensure eventual service. 2) Dynamic queue timeouts: configurable soft and hard timeouts at queue and request level; soft timeout triggers early flush/partial-batch dispatch, hard timeout forces eviction to avoid unbounded waiting. 3) Starvation prevention heuristics: when one queue accumulates beyond a threshold we enforce short, periodic priority boosts to other queues and allow preemption-friendly batch formation. 4) KV-cache pinning follow-up: while not changing pinning semantics, scheduler now considers cached-KV hits when scoring requests so that requests with warm KV are favored where appropriate. 5) Metrics + observability: added per-queue histograms for wait_time, age, starved_count, forced_flush_count, and a new tracing tag for timeout_reason. 6) Runtime knobs: introduce config flags continuous_batcher.queue.timeout_soft_ms, .timeout_hard_ms, .aging_increment_ms, and .starvation_threshold_count with safe defaults.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks and e2e perf harness show median latency unchanged and p95/p99 improved by ~12-18% on the mixed-small/large workload profile used in bench lab. Throughput stays within 3% of baseline. See bench results in commits.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged default on in canary nodes for 2 weeks, monitor metrics (starved_count, forced_flush_count, p99 latency). If regressions observed, revert via feature flag. We will also ship recommended tuning guide in docs.

Tests: Unit tests for aging math and timeout logic added, simulation harness for multi-queue starvation scenarios, integration e2e perf test included. CI runs full unit + integration + e2e-perf.

Notes: Config defaults chosen conservatively (soft=40ms, hard=250ms) to avoid prematurely flushing large batches on latency-sensitive flows. We will iterate defaults after canary telemetry.

review_comments: Alex Kim: Can you explain how the aging increment was chosen? Would a high cardinality of queues cause unfair boosts?

Samir Patel: Answered: chosen from synthetic sweep (10-100ms) and real-customer traces; aging is additive and clipped to avoid runaway priority; high-cardinality queues get proportional aging based on queue length so no single queue dominates.
Priya Nair: Please add a metric for forced_flush_count and a dashboard panel to correlate with p99 latency.
Samir Patel: Added forced_flush_count metric and included a sample Grafana panel in docs. Also added tracing tag to debug timeout_reason.
Jordan Lee: Integration test flaky on first run (timing). Can we make tests less wall-clock sensitive?
Samir Patel: Adjusted tests to use deterministic simulated clock where possible and increased timeouts in e2e harness; re-ran CI and confirmed stability.
Alex Kim: Approved after verifying bench results and code comments. Priya approved on second pass.

bench_summary: Mixed workload bench: baseline p99=710ms -> tuned p99=625ms (12% improvement); p95 improved from 210ms -> 185ms. Throughput -2.3% under 95% CI.
changelog_entry: Improve continuous-batcher scheduler fairness and add queue timeouts to prevent starvation (non-breaking).
security_considerations: No new secrets or auth surfaces. Timeout-related changes do not alter request headers or data handling. Metrics exposed are operational only.
backwards_compatibility: No API changes to public endpoints; runtime-only config knobs with safe defaults. Backwards compatible.
additional_notes: Follow-up work: (1) Auto-tune aging parameters from production telemetry, (2) Evaluate preemption trade-offs for low-latency tails, (3) Add support for tenant-weighted fairness.
